sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang begins over Orchestra row J, so seats from there back can lose the top of the stage, more noticeably from around row M.
sn.sh: Overhang trims the top of the stage from row J back

sn.c: In the Left and Right Orchestra, the side of the stage gets more restricted the further out you sit, and seats on the far side aisles are hit hardest.
sn.sh: Far side Orchestra seats lose part of the stage

sn.c: The Balcony overhang starts over Mezzanine row D and is more noticeable in the back half, though views there are still decent.
sn.sh: Balcony overhang from row D, stronger at the back

sn.c: The Left Balcony can feel steep and cramped. Anyone needing more room should aim for row A or an inside aisle seat.
sn.sh: Steep and cramped, row A or inside aisle helps

sn.c: Center Balcony seats are the cheapest in the theater, and row A adds extra legroom and the clearest view on this level.
sn.sh: Cheapest level, and row A has legroom and clear views

vs.sum: The St. James Theatre offers good sightlines for most seats, though the lack of a solid rake can be an issue if someone tall sits in front of you. The sound quality is generally good, but the tight legroom can be uncomfortable for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic and grand interior, while facilities are average with standard amenities.

acc.note: No steps from sidewalk to Orchestra. No elevator. Mezzanine up 29 steps, Balcony up 76 steps.
